attempts.bug_summary: When forced content-type handling is enabled and both a content type and character encoding are configured, the response encoding is applied before the content type. Setting the content type afterward can replace or discard the previously selected charset, causing the response to use an incorrect character encoding.

The method now rejects null selectors, requests, and responses before constructing the web exchange. However, when the view has no selector of its own, an empty caller-provided selector set is passed through to the template engine instead of being normalized to null, causing empty-selector fragment processing rather than full-template processing.

The web exchange is initialized with the default charset instead of the charset selected from the requested content type. When a content type specifies a non-default charset, the rendering context and generated response can use inconsistent encodings.

Path variables are merged after the explicitly supplied model, so a path variable with the same name overrides the caller's model attribute. This only changes behavior when both sources provide the same key.

When a view name contains named fragment parameters, the method installs the merged model as the expression context variables instead of installing the parameters extracted from the fragment expression. As a result, fragment parameter values are not available under their declared names during template processing, particularly when they differ from or are absent in the regular model.

The merged model gives path variables precedence over controller-provided render attributes when both sources define the same key. This can cause a template to receive a path value instead of the explicitly supplied model value, particularly when rendering a view with colliding attribute names.

When the supplied content type does not specify a charset, the method consults any charset already present on the response before using the view's configured default. This lets prior response state override the fallback required for the rendering content type, causing template processing to use an unintended charset.

Data-driven mode detection uses only controller-supplied render attributes when that map is present, excluding data-driver variables contributed by static view variables or URI path variables. A data-driven template in those sources can therefore be rendered through the non-data-driven response path, changing flushing and execution behavior.

When a standard dialect is configured with an explicitly supplied prefix, the returned configuration records the dialect's default prefix instead of the configured one. Processor registration still uses the explicit prefix, so the stored standard-dialect metadata can disagree with the processors that were actually aggregated.

Execution-attribute conflicts are checked against an entry's value rather than its name. As a result, dialects that define the same attribute under different values are incorrectly rejected in some cases, while duplicate attribute names can overwrite silently when their values do not happen to match an existing key.

The processing order of queued models is reversed around delegation to the next handler. This causes models intended to run before the standalone element to execute afterward, while models intended to run afterward execute first, affecting tags where both queues are populated or where delegation observes the modified context.

attempts.bug_summary: When throttling is enabled, a standalone tag with only an insert-before model is processed immediately instead of being wrapped in the resumable processable used for queued execution. This bypasses throttled flow-control handling for the before-model path and can cause delegation or context-level updates to occur despite a stop state raised while that model is processed.

The model-processor path applies its context changes through the tag structure handler rather than the model structure handler. Consequently, local-variable or inlining changes requested by an element model processor are not propagated when a standalone element is processed through the gathered-model flow.

attempts.bug_summary: When both before-model content and a non-processable after-model are present, the after-model is routed through the processor handler instead of the downstream handler. This can cause inserted after-content to undergo unintended processor execution when a separate processor has also inserted content before the element.

Adjacent expressions occurring after an earlier literal substitution are treated as though they are still part of the substitution. This introduces an unnecessary empty-string concatenation into otherwise independent expressions.

When an escape-prefix character is repeated inside a literal substitution, the implementation treats every prefix after the first as already escaped and does not preserve the required escaping for the generated text literal. This affects substitutions containing consecutive backslashes while leaving ordinary text and single escape prefixes unchanged.

Nested expression unwinding incorrectly marks the parser as being outside an expression when an inner expression closes. This can cause a subsequent nested expression opener to be processed as a top-level expression, corrupting state for nested expression sequences within a substitution.

When a value is surrounded by commas and reaches the end of the sequence, the handler receives the content span as the value's outer span as well. This causes the delimiters to be omitted from the outer value metadata while the content itself remains unchanged.

For quoted values that begin on a different line from their operator, the reported value location is taken from the operator instead of the value start. Same-line quoted values and all unquoted values retain their normal locations, so the defect only appears when quoting and line transitions interact.

The filter failure shows that the earlier candidate was detected because the unterminated quoted-value test expected a TextParseException, but the supplied execution indicates that path returned normally; the feedback does not establish that the value-location change itself caused the exception difference. This version instead records the operator location from the locator after operator scanning, so attributes whose operators are followed by additional operator characters or whitespace receive an end-of-operator position rather than the operator's starting position.
